title: Projective dimension bound over a finite-variable polynomial ring over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $m\geq0$ be an integer, and put $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Every $S$-module $N$, without any finite-generation or grading hypothesis, has a projective resolution of length at most $m$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]: there is an exact sequence $0\to P_m\to\cdots\to P_0\to N\to0$ in which each $P_j$ is projective. For $m=0$ this says that every $k$-vector space is projective. No finiteness of the $P_j$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), second sentence: a polynomial algebra in m variables over a field has global dimension m. Only the upper bound is used.

proof.text: Put $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], $S$ is Noetherian and every prime localization is regular local. For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$, [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] gives $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-finite-gl-dim] to this regular local ring with $d=m$: every $S_{\mathfrak q}$-module has a projective resolution of length at most $m$. The bound is the same for every $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), proof via Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space) and Tag 00O7 (proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim).

proof.text: Let $M$ be a finitely generated $S$-module. For every maximal $\mathfrak q$, apply Step 1 to the localized module $M_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-ext-degree] its bounded resolution implies the Ext-vanishing predicate $\mathrm{PD}_{\leq m}(M_{\mathfrak q})$ used in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-pd-local-global]. Since $S$ is commutative Noetherian and $M$ is finitely generated, the reverse implication of that local-to-global statement gives $\mathrm{PD}_{\leq m}(M)$. Apply the reverse implication of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-resolution-ext-degree] to obtain an actual projective resolution of $M$ of length at most $m$. Choose a universe containing the rings and modules throughout; the bridge applies in $\mathrm{ModuleCat}^{\max(u,v)}$.

source.place: Tag 00O9 (lemma-finite-gl-dim-primes), converse proof, using the existing fixed-bound Mathlib local-to-global criterion and Tag 065R (lemma-projective-dimension-ext).

proof.text: Step 2 proves condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-global-dimension-finite-modules-suffice] for $R=S$ and $n=m$. Its implication (2) to (1) gives a projective resolution of length at most $m$ for every $S$-module $N$, with no finite-generation hypothesis. Unpack [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] to obtain precisely $0\to P_m\to\cdots\to P_0\to N\to0$ with each $P_j$ projective. Neither the cited implication nor this definition imposes finiteness on these projectives.

source.place: Tag 00O9 (lemma-finite-gl-dim-primes), converse conclusion using Tag 065T (lemma-finite-gl-dim); Tag 00OQ, upper-bound assertion.

proof.text: When $m=0$, the polynomial-ring definition [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] identifies $S$ with $k$: the only monomial has all exponents zero. The resolution in Step 3 is $0\to P_0\to N\to0$, so its middle map is an isomorphism. A direct-summand presentation of $P_0$ in a free module gives one for $N$ by composing its inclusion with this inverse and its retraction with this isomorphism. Thus $N$ is projective by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. This also covers the zero module; no grading was introduced at any step.
